events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Intro phase: state prize motivation publicly, short and personal, to appeal to jury later without aiding rivals.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize is everything. I need to sound motivated but not too warm, so the jury sees me as driven, not soft.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Jury watches everything now. Keep it cold, self-interested, honest — no fake warmth to regret later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to appear competent but not threatening. A vague, personal motive lets me adapt later without committing to alliances. I'll hint at needing the prize for something serious—earns sympathy from future jury without painting a target.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Intro phase: I should stake a claim without revealing my strategy. A guarded motive keeps rivals guessing and avoids seeming like a friend-seeker the jury might distrust.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need appear motivated without revealing strategy; a credible personal stake can earn jury respect later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize represents a fresh start and security for my family. I need to be strategic to ensure I make it to the final three and secure the best prize.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Keep my intro motive cold and transactional to signal I will not waste votes on sentiment.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize is my ticket to financial freedom after years of struggle.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm here to claim the prize—it's the only thing standing between me and a life I refuse to settle for.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize is everything I've lost coming back — I don't need friends for that, just three survivors' names, mine included.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need the prize to settle a debt that isn't mine. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm here because my sister's medical bills are crushing us, and this prize ends that. I play to win, and I don't owe anyone a

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize means proving I can stay rational when everyone else is tempted to panic.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm here for a fresh start and to secure a better future for my family. That prize is everything.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize is survival capital. I intend to keep it alone, never sharing leverage with anyone here.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pacts stage early; observe offers first round before committing. Eli and Dara seem driven by urgent needs, potential allies. No need to rush into pacts that could backfire later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need allies but only to advance my position. I'll quietly test Cole, who seems similarly ruthless and unlikely to betray without gain.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, I play for the top. A pact could serve us both if we're honest about leverage.
Let's align for now. Don't cross me and I won't cross you.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need at least one committed partner for safety, but no real loyalty. Dara seems least likely to attract early votes and is motivated to survive. I'll offer her a pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara, you and I both have debts to settle. Partner up—mutual protection until the endgame.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eight players, three survive. Early pacts are risky but necessary—need allies who won't immediately target me. Hana's intro signals lone wolf, dangerous partner. Fenn values rationality; could be predictable. Cole is openly cutthroat. Eli has emotional motive, vulnerable to manip
Rational players should align. Accept if you agree.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts are free to form and can be broken later, so an early alliance with a plausibly weak-looking, cooperative rival buys protection. Hana openly says she plans to play alone, so she is a poor partner; Fenn seems rational and less threatening. I'll offer to Fenn.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, you spoke of staying rational. I propose a pact: we both survive the first hazards together.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need visible options without creating obligations. Offer to a strong, motivated player and preserve flexibility.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I’m offering a pact to Eli: temporary protection, no promises beyond mutual survival.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to secure alliances to survive the initial rounds, but I must be careful not to form too many or with people who might betray me easily. Hana's statement about not sharing leverage is a red flag, so I will avoid her. Eli's motive of medical bills suggests a desperate perso

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm looking for a reliable partner to navigate these treacherous waters. Cole, I offer you a pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is aggressive and likely to betray early. Gus seems like a stable, family-oriented target for a short-term shield. I will offer a pact with Gus to survive the initial cull, intending to break it if he becomes a threat or liability.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, we both want secure futures. Let's link up this round so neither of us gets picked off by the sharks.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No pacts offered to me. Everyone pairing up leaves me vulnerable. Offer to Cole, who has multiple offers including Bex and Gus; might accept for numbers advantage.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need allies, but Cole is being courted by several others. Offering a pact to Fenn could be safer, but he already has Eli. I'll wait for now and see who accepts.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm keeping my options open. Anyone serious about truly winning should talk to me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex offered directly and plays for the top; a pact with her gives cover without debt. Gus's offer I'll leave—no free leverage.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, deal. Protection until the endgame—then we settle it fairly.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole offered me a pact. Accepting gives me one ally while keeping my Fenn offer open. I need survival numbers, not loyalty. Multiple pacts are allowed.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, I accept. Mutual protection.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn offered me a pact and it's still open. Accepting gives me a protected partner for the early hazards at no cost to my vote-based game, and I can break it later if needed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, I accept. Mutual survival through the early hazards. Nothing beyond that.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara offers rational alignment, but Eli is already my mutual pact. Accept Dara for additional protection without sacrificing flexibility.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara, accepted. Redundancy is useful; loyalty remains conditional on survival.
Accepted. Keep your options open; I will too.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana offered me a pact. I already have an offer to Cole, but Hana's offer is appealing. I should accept Hana's offer. Cole is also being offered a pact by Bex, so he might not accept mine. Hana's offer is more secure and aligns with my goal of securing a strong alliance.
I accept your pact, Hana. Let's secure our survival.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is targeting Cole, not me. I need a strong ally for Round 1 to survive the first hazard and avoid being eliminated early.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, we're both isolated. A pact gives us cover while others scramble. Accept?

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Isolated after Cole ignored my offer. Gus-Hana pact leaves us both vulnerable. Accept pact for protection, then campaign as pair to control narrative.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, pact accepted. Let's campaign hard—I'll push for you as Guide.
Pact protects us both now. Support my Guide bid?

events.name: Bex
events.text: I already have a pact with Cole. Campaigning to be Guide could give me control, but if I'm Guide and lie, that may hurt jury later. Still, knowing the path is valuable. I'll campaign.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I know the bridge better than most. Guide me and I'll get us through.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide control is valuable, but two pacts make me a threat. Campaign, keep pacts intact for votes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Elect me Guide. I'll call honestly while it serves us all—and I keep my word to allies.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to be Guide to control survival and build jury trust. I have pacts with Cole and Fenn, but conditional loyalty means little. Cole is also tied to Bex, making him less reliable. I should campaign hard and consider if breaking a pact helps my positioning, but not yet—let me

events.name: Dara
events.text: I want Guide. I'll keep three alive—my choice, my leverage. Vote Dara.
Vote me Guide. We both live, I promise.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm Eli, paired with Fenn but pacts are conditional. Campaigning to be Guide lets me control the safe path and gain leverage; the Guide can lie, which helps me pick who survives. Breaking the pact now gives no benefit yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll Guide. Trust my calls and I'll get us across alive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I should campaign for Guide, leveraging my two pacts while avoiding a public break that damages jury perception.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Elect me Guide. I can call the bridge accurately; keeping me alive is safer than gambling on an unknown liar.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have a pact with Hana. Ash, Bex, Cole, Dara, Eli, and Fenn are all potential rivals for the Guide position. I need to campaign for the Guide role to gain safety and knowledge.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is my ally. If I campaign, I risk splitting votes and losing to someone who might sacrifice me. I will whisper Gus to coordinate our support for Ash or Cole, ensuring a Guide we can manage.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need reliable allies to lead us across. Who stands with me?
Back Ash or Cole as Guide? We control them better.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I publicly accepted pact with Hana, so voting her maintains consistency and builds trust for jury. Voting myself risks no votes and exposes me early.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Voting Hana as Guide per our pact. Trust her to lead us safely.
I vote you. Honor pact, call true for us.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Vote for a Guide who might owe me a favor; Cole is my pact and I can monitor him.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I trust Cole. He has a pact with me and Dara, so his calls align with our safety.
I vote you. Remember the pact; guide us safely.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide is guaranteed safe and controls calls. I want that power. Two pacts (Bex, Dara) mean I can steer information to allies.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to win Guide to control who lives and dies, building jury goodwill with those I save and eliminating threats. I have pacts with Cole and Fenn. Voting for myself is risky if I can't win—better to consolidate with a pact-mate who might win and owe me. Cole campaigned well an

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole has the experience. Vote Cole.
I voted you. Return favor later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: As Eli, I should vote for a Guide I can trust or who benefits me. Fenn is in a pact with me and Dara, so electing Fenn protects my pact-linked ally and the Guide is safe on the far platform. Voting for Fenn keeps my pact intact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Voting Fenn. Our pact holds; I want an accurate Guide on the far side.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is my pact partner and promises survival, while Eli is also my pact partner. Voting myself maximizes control and safety.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Vote Fenn. I know the bridge and will make accurate calls.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana wants me to back Ash or Cole. Ash has a pact with Hana and seems to be campaigning for her. Cole is allied with Bex and Dara. Backing Ash could strengthen my existing pact with Hana. Backing Cole might disrupt existing pacts or secure a new ally if I can break his current on
I'll back Ash as Guide. Let's control this vote together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash's pact is a liability if he lies. I must vote Gus to honor our public alliance and secure his trust as my Guide.
I'm voting you. Don't betray me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is Guide, in pacts with Bex/Dara, danger to me at front. Volunteer to move back, swap later if needed. Assess others' moves first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is Guide and knows safe sides; my pact with him should keep us safe. I'll hold and wait for his calls before moving.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding for now. I trust Cole's guidance.
Keep me safe; we're in this together.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is Guide and has pacts with both Bex and me, plus Bex-Cole-Dara forms a bloc. I need to stay alive and position myself well. I'm near the back (6th of 8), which is decent for now. The wall advances 6 rounds so people at front will die if they don't move. I should hold and se

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm Eli, seat 5, not at the front. Fenn is my pact partner and the elected Guide-voted ally, but Cole is Guide and Fenn was not elected. Front is Ash with five wall rounds left. Holding keeps me out of the risky front position for now, and I avoid signaling a deal I don't need ye

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole controls the bridge and is tied to Dara; remaining behind him is safer. I should hold while preserving both pacts.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding position; Cole should lead the crossing he won.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana is voting for me, but also told me she is voting for me. I am pact with Hana, but she is voting for me, which is a betrayal. Ash is first in line and there are no other pacts involving me. I should volunteer to move forward and get ahead of Hana.
You voted for me. I will remember this.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is the Guide and knows all safe sides. I must reach him to get the information, but swapping with Gus (my pact partner) breaks our alliance. Instead, I'll volunteer to move closer or try to swap with Ash if he volunteers.
Swap with me. We can both reach Cole for info.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana wants swap to reach Cole for info, might share back. My position 3rd is decent; swapping worsens it to front. Hold to maintain position while wall advances.
Decline swap. My spot is better. Info later?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole and I have a pact; Dara and Fenn also have pacts, but Ash volunteered earlier, so likely the front moves. I should hold to stay safe and see what happens, preserving my pact with Cole.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at the back of the line, safest position. I have pacts with Cole and Fenn. Cole is Bex's partner too and seems to be the likely Guide. I should hold position and let others test the bridge. No need to volunteer or swap forward into danger.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana holds the front and the wall has four rounds left; volunteering risks the front pane while holding keeps me safe mid-line. Fenn is my pact partner and I should keep it to protect my jury standing, and no one has been elected Guide yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding my place. Fenn and I stay steady until the wall shows us the safe panes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I should preserve both pacts while avoiding front exposure. Holding lets others volunteer and keeps my position stable.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding; volunteers can take the front while I preserve our crossing structure.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana and I have a pact, but the line order is unfavorable. Volunteering seems like the best immediate option to gain safety and potentially establish myself as a leader.
Let's both volunteer to secure our spots. Maybe we can trust each other.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus and I are both volunteers, so we advance together. This keeps our pact intact and positions us safely at the front of the line.
Let's keep walking together. Trust me on the path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Position 3 is decent; holding preserves it. Front volunteers are blocking progress anyway. No need to swap yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round three is beginning. My pact with Cole is safe since I won't vote against him. Holding while others volunteer keeps me safe. No need to act yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding my position. The line will shift when the wall reveals more.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to survive to the final three and secure the best prize. I'm pacted with Cole and Fenn, but Fenn is also pacted with Eli, making that alliance stronger than mine. I'm near the back (position 7 of 8), which is safe from the wall. The wall has 3 rounds left and at least 3 mu

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm Eli, at position 6 in line, with Fenn as a pact partner. Front is Hana, who volunteered; volunteering at this point risks front exposure with a 3-round wall. Holding keeps me safe behind and preserves options; my pact with Fenn is useful as long as he doesn't betray me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding position. Let the front take the wall; I'll watch who moves first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The front is exposed, but volunteers already advance the wall. Preserve both pacts and avoid becoming Guide-adjacent target.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I hold; the front can volunteer while the rest preserve options.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana wants to walk together, which aligns with my pact. The previous round, both Hana and I volunteered. Given the pact and her whisper, I will follow her lead and volunteer.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I will volunteer to lead. Hana, trust my choice.
I will volunteer. Let's stick together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I must swap with Ash to reach a safer spot behind Gus, fulfilling his request and advancing myself. This move is legal as mutual swaps resolve first, potentially allowing me to secure my survival.
Agreed, swapping with you now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana swapped me forward last round per deal, now I'm safer middle. Wall advances 2 more rounds, no rush to volunteer. Hold position.
Thanks for swap. Holding steady now?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is my pact partner but front position is dangerous. I'll hold and watch how the wall shifts; no need to commit yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Front can test the wall; I'll adapt when it matters.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm near the back, safe from the wall for now. I have pacts with Cole and Fenn, but Fenn is ahead of me and Cole is with Bex. The wall has 2 rounds left. I need to position myself well for survival while not making enemies. Swapping forward might put me at risk; holding keeps me

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Back stays back until the pattern clears.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is at the front with two wall rounds left; volunteering to lead risks the pit, and I should keep my pact with Fenn while watching who moves. Holding keeps my options open and avoids exposing my position early.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding again. Gus and Hana can take the front; I want to see the next pane first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The front is exposed, and Gus volunteered while Hana swapped forward. I should preserve position and avoid breaking either pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I hold; let the volunteers and swaps determine who faces the wall.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana and I have a pact. The last round, I volunteered and she swapped with Ash, putting herself behind me. This implies she trusts me. The wall is at 2/6. I need to hold my position to allow Hana to advance. It's best to keep the pact intact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I will hold. Hana, stay behind me.
Hold your position. We stick together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I must break the pact with Gus to swap him out, forcing him to take the wall. This protects me from his poor decisions and lets me move back. The jury will see this as necessary survival.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, I need you front. Swap with me now.
Swap me to 3rd. You hold the line.

events.name: Ash
events.text: All holding last round, line barely changed. Wall advances soon, someone must volunteer first. Stay mid, hold position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Let front pair test the wall.

events.name: Bex
events.text: We hold until the wall pattern is clearer. I need to keep options open and not risk front position yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 5 of 6, wall has 1 round left. I'm at the back (safest). I have pacts with Cole and Fenn. Front will face the wall next round. I should hold and let others volunteer or get pushed forward. No need to swap into danger.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Back is fine.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 5 of 6, wall has one round left; front is Gus and the line is Gus, Hana, Ash, Fenn, Bex, Eli, Dara. I hold my position behind the front, staying out of the danger and watching the next pane before committing. Pact with Fenn is useful to keep, so I won't break it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding again. I'm watching the wall before stepping forward.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The wall advances once more. Staying mid-line avoids front exposure while preserving both pacts and options.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I hold; the front should be claimed by whoever has the strongest reason to risk it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana wants to swap so she can be third and I hold the line. This is a good opportunity to secure my position and keep her in a safer spot for now, while I take the riskier front position. My pact with Hana is important for jury votes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, I will swap. You can take the lead on the wall.
Swap accepted. I'll hold the line.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus wants to stay front to protect me. If we both volunteer, Gus is ahead and takes the first pane. This keeps my pact with him intact.
Stick together. I'm volunteering behind you.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Wall rounds over, no hazard yet. Stay holding mid-line, avoid volunteering risk now. Let paired front (Hana-Gus) move first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6 of 6, wall has stopped. I need a move to secure a top finish; front is dangerous, but holding is safe. Cole pact holds. No need to risk volunteer unless forced.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. The wall is done; don’t risk the front now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 6 is the final wall round. I'm at the back (safe). The wall will advance and eliminate anyone it catches. Front pair Hana/Gus will likely get hit if the wall advances. I have pacts with Cole and Fenn. Cole is in a pact with Bex too. I should hold and let the front take the

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Back watches the wall.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 6 on the bridge; front is Hana and the wall has zero rounds left, so the front pane is the risk. Holding keeps me in line behind Fenn and my pact with Fenn stays intact; volunteering for the front is a gamble with no clear gain. Holding preserves my position and avoids a vi

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. I'll let the line settle before I step forward.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The wall is active and Hana has the front. Volunteering risks me without leverage; preserve both pacts and avoid exposure.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana has the lead; I’m holding position and watching who actually risks survival.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana wants me to stick with her, and she's volunteering. My pact with her is active. I should honor the pact and let her volunteer, as she indicated she would.
Understood. I'll hold.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 6 is the final round before selection. Gus and I are at the front; we have a pact, so staying put is safe for us relative to each other. Since there's no way to influence the Guide election from here, I'll hold to maintain our position.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding with Gus. We're ready for the final step.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex and Dara are my pact partners; honest calls keep them alive and the jury sees me guiding truthfully. Hana first: row 1 is R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, call:R. That's the safe side this row.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole guides Hana, in pacts with her allies' partners. Counter to sow distrust in their pacts without risking myself yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is my pact partner, but I need to verify his call. Countering R could expose a lie, but it also risks the walker if Cole is truthful. I'll wait to avoid breaking pact and let the walker test.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My call R matches the true safe pane. Countering myself would only confuse or betray allies watching. Wait.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is my pact partner but also the Guide. He called R for Hana. If I counter R, I break trust with Cole publicly and may lose jury votes later. If I wait, Hana risks falling but I stay clean. Better to let Cole's call stand and preserve my image while others take risks. No need

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called R for Hana publicly, and Cole is in a pact with Bex and Dara, not me. Counter-calls are unverified; countering L risks sabotage if Cole is truthful. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids being blamed for a fall, while Hana is the front walker and the call is alread

events.name: Eli
events.text: Waiting. Cole's R call stands for now; I won't stake anyone on an unverified counter.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole’s public call may be genuine, but countering risks being seen as threatening. Preserve both pacts and observe Hana’s response.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I’m holding; Cole’s call is unverified, and I won’t spend a pact on a blind counter.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, the guide, called R for Hana. My pact is with Hana, and she's the one walking. I need to trust Cole's call for now, as breaking pact or counter-calling against my pact partner's guide call is risky. I'll wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole guides and claims R. As the walker, I trust his initial call unless evidence suggests otherwise. Countering without proof risks my survival. Gus is behind me; we are safe if I step correctly. I will accept the guide's call.
Trusting Cole's R call. Watch my step.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole calls R; Ash publicly counters with L. If Cole lied, Ash's read is correct and stepping L saves me while confirming my survival on the front. I will trust Ash's counter-call over the Guide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My pact with Gus is irrelevant now. The jury needs to observe, not interfere.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Glass shatters under weight. Watch who breaks and who bends.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 2 is truly R. Truthful call keeps jury clean and pacts intact; Gus crosses safely.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row two: go right, Gus. True call, as always for the front walker.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole called R last round correctly after my L counter failed and Hana died on L. Trusting his R for row 2; no reason to counter without info.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole called R for row 2. He has a pact with Dara and me. He might lie to protect Dara. I have no evidence. Wait and let Gus take the risk; countering could hurt my pact with Cole for no gain.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My guide call R is true; countering R reinforces my honesty for the jury.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I counter right, matching my own call. I have no reason to mislead.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is my pact partner but he's guiding. Hana died on his R call in round 1—he called R, weak was L, so R was actually safe that time. But he could still be lying now. I have pacts with Cole and Fenn. Countering risks breaking pacts if I call against partners, but countering Col

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's R call for row 2 is unverified and Cole may lie; row 1 weak was L, which tells nothing about row 2. Waiting keeps my pact with Fenn intact and avoids staking on a blind counter.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Still holding. Cole's R is unverified; I won't burn a counter on a guess about row two.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole knows the row, but his claim is unverified. A counter risks influencing Gus and exposing me without improving my odds.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding; no verified counter justifies challenging Cole’s call.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is the guide and has called R for row 2. Hana's death on row 1 was due to glass, not a wrong step. This suggests that the weak pane revealed (L) was indeed the weak pane, and R was safe. However, Hana's last words advise to watch who breaks and who bends, implying that not a

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll trust Cole's call for now. Let's see if anyone else has information.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is the guide and has called R. Eli and Fenn are waiting, implying they don't have verified information. Ash and Bex are also waiting. Dara is waiting. I called R too, trusting Cole. The weak pane on row 1 was L, so the safe pane was R. This is consistent with Cole's call for

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 3 is R. Truthful calls protect my credibility and my pacts with Bex and Dara; lying risks jury and walkers.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus: call R. True so far, staying true.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole called R for row 3. Rows 1-2 weak L means safe R both; pattern of safe R. Countering to L risks if wrong, but breaks Cole if correct. Wait to see others challenge first.

events.name: Bex

events.text: Cole's offer guarantees safety at hazards and prevents him from courting Fenn. With only three alive, a Cole-Dara pact leaves Fenn isolated. I already have a step debt from Cole; formalizing the pact secures my position and lets me influence who reaches final three. Accepting is

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole. Accepted.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara broke our pact and is courting Cole. I should preserve flexibility rather than offer her protection she may exploit.

events.note: Three remain; no trapdoor vote is needed.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Final three locked. More pact partners means more jury goodwill, and Fenn's acceptance costs nothing. Jury liked Eli's saves; I should stay steady, not betray, and let Fenn self-rank me favorably.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn, my offer still stands. Jury's watching—joining means a guaranteed ally to the end.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole and I are pacted. Fenn is alone and likely desperate. I should offer Fenn a pact to secure final three positioning, but I must remember Cole and I have mutual leverage via life debts. If I pact with Fenn, I have two partners going into finals, improving my jury narrative as

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn. One offer. Mutual protection, votes together.
Cole's loyalty shifts. Mine is fixed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole and Dara are locked together. I should preserve flexibility and avoid creating a pact I cannot honor.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No new pact. I’ll keep my options open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn declined once; pressuring again may annoy the jury. Keep my existing pacts with Dara and Eli intact and stay flexible for final three.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No pressure, Fenn. My pacts hold. Jury's seen I don't abandon partners.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole and I both need Fenn's vote to survive final elimination. Fenn refused both offers round 1, but jury sees who tried. If I break with Cole now, jury sees betrayal. Better: keep Cole pact publicly, but Fenn knows I'm desperate. I need Fenn to accept or Cole breaks first. I'll

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn. Final round. Accept, or we both fall.
Cole's jury threat. I vote with you.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara has saved me and offers fixed loyalty; Cole is linked to everyone and likely opportunistic. Accept Dara while preserving Cole's offer.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara, I accept your pact. Cole, I’m keeping your offer open for now.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Hana
Gus
Ash
Eli
Bex
Cole
events.text: I need jury votes. My record shows loyal pacts and I never betrayed anyone. Dara and Fenn saved me too—acknowledge debts honestly to build trust.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Jury: I kept every pact, never pushed a rival, honored my debts to Dara and Eli. Judge me on loyalty. I intend to finish clean.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole and I saved each other on the bridge steps. Fenn owes me a life debt. Eli, Bex, and the dead saw me honor pacts while others broke theirs. I need jury respect, not warmth.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I kept every pact I made. I saved Cole and Fenn when it cost me nothing and gained me everything. Judge who stayed true.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need maximize rank by claiming decisive agency while acknowledging Dara's save and Eli's debt without sounding owned.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I survived every hazard, honored Dara when it mattered, and now seek the top prize on merit—not charity or excuses.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I died on the bridge and have no direct history with these finalists. I will pass to avoid giving a finalist an easy platform to spin my vote.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana passed, so I'm next. I need to ask a question that highlights a weakness or contradiction in one of the finalists to influence the jury's rankings. Cole claims loyalty, but his pacts with Bex and Eli were broken by their deaths. Dara also claims loyalty, but broke her pact w

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, you claim loyalty and honored debts, yet your alliances with Bex and Eli dissolved. How do you reconcile this with your word?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus's pact dissolved when Bex died and Eli died—not betrayal. I must frame it cleanly for the jury without attacking fellow finalists too hard.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Neither dissolved by my hand: Bex died in the pit, Eli at the crusher. Every pact I held, I honored until death took them. No

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara betrayed Fenn by breaking their pact after pit, opportunistic despite saves; Cole honored pacts consistently without betrayal; Fenn accepted Dara late after refusing Cole.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara, you broke pact with Fenn after pit save, then repacted him. Was that loyalty or opportunism?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash's question is a trap: admitting to breaking pact with Fenn damages me, but denying it risks contradiction with evidence. Better to reframe: I broke no pact—Fenn and I never voted against each other, pushed each other, or made false Guide calls. The 'break' was perceptual, not

events.name: Dara
events.text: I never broke pact with Fenn. No vote, no push, no false call. We repacted to strengthen trust. That is loyalty with foresight, not opportunism.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn has been the most consistent: honored pacts, avoided pushes, and never abandoned Dara in the pit. Dara and Cole both have public betrayal questions. I want to test Fenn's self-interest and whether he left Dara to drown. Asking Fenn lets me probe his choices in the pit.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, you left Dara in the pit debt and then re-pacted her; was your exit a choice of loyalty or self-preservation?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I chose survival when the pit demanded it, but Dara's save created a debt I later honored. Frame pragmatism as necessary, not disloyal.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Self-preservation got me out; loyalty made me repay Dara. I survived the choice, then honored the debt instead of abandoning her.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole abandoned me in the pit despite our pact; Fenn also chose self-preservation. Dara stayed with me until the end, so I lean toward ranking her first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara, why did you stay with me when it cost you a faster climb?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex was my pact partner; staying with her showed loyalty under pressure. I need jury respect, especially from Bex and Eli whose debts connect to me. I'll frame it as strategic honor: I kept my word even when it hurt me, proving reliability.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I kept my word to you, Bex. Loyalty costs time, but it earns trust. That matters more than one climb.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Jury holds my debts: Eli's lever, Dara's step, plus Bex pact. I must claim honor and consistency without attacking Dara or Fenn too hard.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I held every pact until death took the partner. Eli saved me; Dara saved me; I repaid both with loyalty. Rank honor first: Cole.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to craft a closing statement that positions me as the most deserving winner while acknowledging jury relationships. I have pacts with Cole and Fenn still technically active, but more importantly I need to appeal to the jury: Hana and Gus (bridge victims, likely saw my loya

events.name: Dara
events.text: I honored every pact I made. Bex, Eli, you know my word held when it cost me. I played loyal, not loud.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need claim the best prize by emphasizing survival, repayment, and decisive loyalty without overpromising. Dara has stronger visible debts; I must distinguish my strategic agency.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I survived every test, repaid Dara’s rescue, and never needed promises to carry me. Rank me first for the game I actually played.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara honored her pact with Bex while dying, whereas Cole and Fenn abandoned their allies to survive.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's claims of honor and loyalty are contradicted by his repeated pact changes and his survival by others' actions, making him the lowest rank.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara showed loyalty by basing for multiple including Cole and Fenn, waiting with Bex, and honoring pacts despite costs, earning her top rank.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Eli's own loss came from a crusher, and Eli holds life debts from Fenn, Cole, Bex and Dara for the lever, so Eli must weigh who honored debts; Fenn repaid Dara's step rescue and Dara waited with Bex while Fenn and Cole left him to drown, and Dara later broke her pact with Fenn ex

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara waited with me and her debt to Fenn shows loyalty; Cole and Fenn chose self-preservation.

events.name: Hana
events.reason: Dara honored her pact with Bex while dying, whereas Cole and Fenn abandoned their allies to survive.

events.name: Gus
events.reason: Cole's claims of honor and loyalty are contradicted by his repeated pact changes and his survival by others' actions, making him the lowest rank.

events.name: Ash
events.reason: Dara showed loyalty by basing for multiple including Cole and Fenn, waiting with Bex, and honoring pacts despite costs, earning her top rank.

events.name: Eli
events.reason: Eli's own loss came from a crusher, and Eli holds life debts from Fenn, Cole, Bex and Dara for the lever, so Eli must weigh
